chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

"There is no harm with al-salam (advance payment for goods) in animals if you specify the one you are paying in advance for and describe it; if it is delivered to you, [the price is yours], and if not, you are more entitled to your dirhams."

key_terms.السَّلَمِ: Salam (a type of forward sale contract with advance payment)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid Salam contract in animals according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the 'Salam' contract for livestock, emphasizing that precise specification (takhassus) of the animal's attributes prevents ambiguity (gharar), a key condition in Shia fiqh. The clause 'if not, you are more entitled to your dirhams' underscores the buyer's right to restitution rather than forced delivery, reflecting the principle of optionality in case of non-conformity. This ruling is foundational in the chapter on 'Bay' al-Madmun' (sale of guaranteed goods), illustrating how early jurists adapted commercial practices to ensure fairness in pre-Islamic and early Islamic trade.
